classification.difficultyReason: Students must express two ground lengths using the unknown height, recognise complementary-angle identities and combine the expressions to prove the supplied formula.

content.prompt:
From a point $P$ due south of a vertical tower, the angle of elevation of the top of the tower is $20^\circ$.

From a point $Q$ 40 metres from $P$ and due east of the tower, the angle of elevation is $35^\circ$.

$h$ is the height of the tower.

Show that $$h=\frac{40}{\sqrt{\tan^2 70^\circ+\tan^2 55^\circ}}$$ and evaluate $h$ to the nearest metre.

spec.description: Tower top and unnamed foot joined to Q and P; QP is 40 m. The foot has a projected ground right-angle mark. Elevation angles are between each ground sightline and the corresponding line to the tower top.
spec.mathematics: The tower is vertical. Ground distances to P and Q are perpendicular; their lengths are h cot 20 degrees and h cot 35 degrees.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied labels and angle givens are visible.

answer.worked:
Let $F$ be the foot of the tower.

$$\begin{aligned}PF&=\frac{h}{\tan20^\circ}=h\tan70^\circ\\QF&=\frac{h}{\tan35^\circ}=h\tan55^\circ\end{aligned}$$

Since $PF\perp QF$, Pythagoras gives

$$\begin{aligned}PF^2+QF^2&=PQ^2\\h^2\tan^2 70^\circ+h^2\tan^2 55^\circ&=40^2\\h^2(\tan^2 70^\circ+\tan^2 55^\circ)&=1600\\h&=\frac{40}{\sqrt{\tan^2 70^\circ+\tan^2 55^\circ}}\\h&\approx13\text{ m}.\end{aligned}$$
